label: Frontiers in Immunology
description: Frontiers in Immunology (Frontiers). A single-journal Frontiers profile: the Article-types page carries the per-type maximum word counts (Original Research 12,000; Review 12,000; Mini Review 3,000; Brief Research Report 4,000; Case Report 3,000; Opinion 2,000; General Commentary 1,000; Conceptual Analysis 8,000; ...), and the profile applies each type's own maximum with no margin (relaxation 1.0). Frontiers publishes no separate abstract word limit, no legend word limit and no cover-letter limit, so those are counted without a cap; the submission system's 200-word scope statement is carried as the venue-level cover-letter preference on top of the operator's 650-word TOTAL-content cap. Frontiers requires an editable Word or LaTeX manuscript, so submission.pdf_accepted is false.

length_limits.source: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/for-authors/article-types, 'Original Research'; https://www.frontiersin.org/guidelines/author-guidelines, 'Abstract' and 'Manuscript length'; both checked 2026-10-01 -- maximum 12,000 words

abstract.note: Frontiers Author guidelines, 'Abstract' (https://www.frontiersin.org/guidelines/author-guidelines, checked 2026-10-01): the abstract is a single structured paragraph (for example IMRAD), abbreviations are minimised and references, figures and tables are not cited in it; the guidelines publish NO separate abstract word limit, so base and relaxation are null and the stages count the abstract without a cap.

main_text.note: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/for-authors/article-types (checked 2026-10-01): the page states a maximum word count of 12,000 for Original Research. Frontiers Author guidelines, 'Manuscript length' (https://www.frontiersin.org/guidelines/author-guidelines, checked 2026-10-01): 'The manuscript length includes only the main body of the text, footnotes, and all citations within it. It excludes the abstract, section titles, figure and table captions, contents of tables and boxes, funding statement, acknowledgments, and references in the bibliography.' The profile applies the venue's own maximum with no margin (relaxation 1.0), because Frontiers states the number as a maximum

cover_letter.source: Frontiers Author guidelines, 'Scope statement' (https://www.frontiersin.org/guidelines/author-guidelines, checked 2026-10-01): 'When you submit your manuscript, you will be required to summarize in 200 words your manuscript's scope and its relevance to the journal and/or specialty section you're submitting to.' Frontiers publishes no cover-letter word limit; this profile carries the submission system's 200-word scope statement as the persuading-part preference. The 650-word total_max is the operator's own TOTAL-content cap (salutation, body, disclosures and signature), not a Frontiers rule

captions.source: Frontiers Author guidelines, 'Captions' and 'Tables' (https://www.frontiersin.org/guidelines/author-guidelines, checked 2026-10-01): 'Captions should be preceded by the appropriate label, for example Figure 1. Figure captions should be placed at the end of the manuscript'; 'Table captions must be placed immediately before the table ... Please use only a single paragraph for the caption'. The guidelines publish no legend WORD limit, so published_limit is null and the stages count legends without a cap (default_cap 0)

submission.pdf_note: Frontiers Author guidelines, 'Templates' and 'Format' (https://www.frontiersin.org/guidelines/author-guidelines, checked 2026-10-01): 'The manuscript should be written using either Word or LaTeX'; 'If you wish to submit your article as LaTeX, we recommend our LaTeX templates ... please ensure all relevant manuscript files are uploaded: .tex file, PDF, and .bib file (if the bibliography is not already included in the .tex file)'. Editors and reviewers only download the PDF the system builds from that source, so a lone PDF is not the manuscript
